Crew: Paramedic Siân Llewellyn-Rhys (collar 4471) / ECA Tomasz "Tom" Wiśniewski (collar 5902)
Receiving unit: Royal Calderbrook Infirmary ED, Majors bay 3 - handed to Sister A. Okonkwo-Bright at 03:37

PATIENT: PARKINSON, Edith ("Edie")   DOB: 03.04.1933 (93yo)   NHS No: 612 498 3307
Home: 7 Weavers Fold, Lower Brackenfold, Hebbleworth BK7 4QT
NOK: grandson Callum Parkinson-Hayes, mob 07700 900 362
GP: Dr R. Hill, Moorside Surgery, tel 01632 960 418

ATMIST
A - 93yo F
T - Unwitnessed fall at home approx 01:30. Call 02:14, on scene 02:41, left scene 03:12.
M - Fell down approx 12 internal stairs, found lying at the foot of the stairs by neighbour. No head strike reported but cannot exclude. Long lie approx 1 hr on tiled floor.
I - R leg shortened + externally rotated, pain R groin 8/10 on movement. 3 cm skin tear L forearm (dressed). No midline C-spine tenderness, Canadian C-spine rule = low risk, collar not applied.
S - HR 104 irreg irreg, BP 98/54, RR 22, SpO2 94% RA, T 35.4, BM 6.8, GCS 14/15 (E4 V4 M6) - disorientated to date only, NEWS2 7.
T - IV 20g L ACF, paracetamol 1 g IV, morphine 2 mg IV x2 (pain down to 4/10), ondansetron 4 mg IV. Scoop + vacuum mattress, warmed blankets. Entonox declined.

BACKGROUND
PMH: Parkinson's disease (dx 2011, on co-careldopa 25/100 QDS - last dose 22:00 yesterday, next due 06:00 - PLEASE PRESCRIBE ON TIME), AF on apixaban, HTN, osteoporosis.
Allergies: penicillin (rash).
SOCIAL: Lives alone, carers x2 daily via Brightwater Homecare (on-call 01632 960 233). Mobilises with Zimmer frame indoors. Neighbour Mr Dennis Fairweather (no. 9) heard a thud, let himself in via the key safe and dialled 999. He reports Edie is "sharp as a tack" normally.
Mrs Parkinson told crew she got up for the toilet in the dark and "missed the second step".

EXTRICATION: Terraced house at the top of a steep cobbled hill - vehicle could not get within 80 m. Hebbleworth Fire & Rescue assisted with the carry down the hill on scoop. Delay on scene approx 20 min.

SAFEGUARDING / REFERRALS: No concerns re: neglect. Falls referral emailed to bk.fallsresponse@nhs.net. Message left on Dr Hill's surgery answerphone. Grandson informed by phone, en route to RCI.

Signed: S. Llewellyn-Rhys, HCPC PA204917, 17/10/2026 03:55

Scene: cnr Voortrekker Rd & Sonderend St, outside Mzansi Cash & Carry. SAPS on scene, Const. Hélène du Toit, case CAS 211/10/2026.

Hx / mechanism: Adult male pedestrian struck by a minibus taxi while crossing the road on foot, walking home after his shift. Witness Ms Precious Arendse (taxi passenger, cell 072 555 8820) estimates taxi speed 50-60 km/h; pt thrown approx 4 m onto tarmac and "lay still for about a minute" before waking up confused. Taxi driver stayed on scene. No alcohol smell. Pt cannot recall the impact.

Primary survey (cABCDE):
c - no catastrophic haemorrhage; ooze from R shin wound controlled with direct pressure.
A - patent, talking. Manual in-line stabilisation, then collar + head blocks (NEXUS positive, distracting injury).
B - RR 24, SpO2 93% RA -> 98% on 15 L/min NRB. Equal air entry, no crepitus, trachea midline.
C - HR 118, BP 142/88, CRT <2 s, skin cool + clammy. Pelvis stable, no binder.
D - GCS 13/15 (E3 V4 M6) on arrival, 14/15 en route. PEARL 3 mm. Amnesic for event. HGT 7.2 mmol/L.
E - Open # R tibia mid-shaft, bone end visible through 3 cm wound, distal pulses + sensation present. Abrasions R forehead and L flank. No Battle's sign, no raccoon eyes.

Mx: 2x IV (18G L ACF, 20G R hand); Ringer's lactate 500 mL; fentanyl 50 mcg IV x2 (pain 9/10 -> 5/10); ondansetron 4 mg IV; wound irrigated with NS, povidone-iodine dressing; vacuum splint R lower leg. Spine board used for extrication only, moved to scoop.

Handover: Tygerkloof Regional Hospital trauma unit, bay T2, 06:18 to Dr Jacobus "Kobus" le Roux (MP 0661347). Wife Nomvula phoned by Mr Baloyi, on her way. Lucky's belongings (cellphone, wallet, Sentinel uniform jacket) handed to Sr. M. Abrahams, property register no. 55/2026.

dialogue:
[paramedic] Right, is everyone ready? This is Desmond White, goes by Des, 64-year-old, date of birth second of March 1962.
[doctor] Go ahead.
[paramedic] Called at 07:52 to Hartwell & Booth Logistics, the depot on Ashworth Lane. He collapsed on the loading bay. A colleague, Mr Kwame Asante-Boateng, said he went white as a sheet and sat down on a pallet clutching his chest. No loss of consciousness.
[doctor] Onset?
[paramedic] Central crushing pain from about half seven, into the jaw and left arm, nine out of ten at worst, now 4/10 after GTN and morphine. Twelve-lead shows ST elevation in II, III and aVF with reciprocal depression in aVL. No Wolff-Parkinson-White pattern. We transmitted it, ref TX-55821-K, and Dr Ferreira on the cath lab accepted, so this is a quick stop for bloods and then straight up.
[doctor] Obs?
[paramedic] First set BP 104/68, heart rate 52 sinus brady, resp 20, sats 95 on air, GCS 15. Last set 112/70, rate 58. Aspirin 300 chewed, one spray of GTN only because of the pressure, morphine 5 milligrams IV in two goes.
[doctor] Background?
[paramedic] Type 2 diabetic on metformin, hypertensive on ramipril, ex-smoker. No allergies.
[doctor] Mr White, how are you feeling now?
[patient] Better than I was, doc. Tell Brenda I'm alright, will you? She'll be going spare.
[nurse] Is Brenda your wife?
[patient] Yeah, forty-one years this Christmas. Her mobile's 07700 900 581.
[paramedic] Jo Pemberton, the site manager, rang her already. She's driving over from Middlehope with their daughter Kerry-Anne.
[doctor] Lovely. Killip class I, let's get him up to the lab.
